hero.headline: New Aldi opens in Hobe Sound as grocery prices rise 2.8% this year
hero.body:
A new Aldi grocery store opened Thursday at 8867 Southeast Bridge Road in Hobe Sound, bringing lower-priced food options to Martin County shoppers facing rising grocery costs. The USDA expects grocery prices to rise 2.8% this year, with fruits and vegetables increasing less than 1%. Pork rose 1% from April to May, chicken prices rose 1.3% over the same period, and wholesale beef prices remain at all-time highs for this time of year, though beef prices fell 1.3% from April to May. Egg prices are dropping.

Customers Cheryl and Tony Cooperman said they are excited to have an affordable option close to their home. "We're thrilled to have it here," Cheryl said. "Now we have something with reasonable prices that's close by." She said grocery prices are getting expensive and are changing the way she shops. "We're the type of people who never used to look at prices," Cheryl said. "I will go with what's on sale instead of just with what we want, and we never used to do that."

Shoppers James and Harry said they do not expect relief at the register anytime soon. "Prices are gonna stay inflated; they're not gonna go down. It's just I'd be willing to bet on that," they said. Still, they said stores like Aldi, which often have lower prices than other stores, can make a difference for everyday shoppers.

"Having stuff like this for the average person is extremely beneficial, because there's nobody who isn't feeling the price increase and stuff," James and Harry said. The new Hobe Sound location provides another shopping option for residents in the northern part of Martin County as food costs continue to put a strain on family budgets.

cards.headline: Two bodies found near Sebastian this week appear unconnected but remain under investigation, sheriff says
cards.body:
The Indian River County Sheriff's Office said Thursday that two bodies found near Sebastian this week appear unconnected, but both deaths remain under investigation. The first body, discovered Monday on the west shoreline near U.S. Highway 1 and the north county line, was identified as James Thompson, 44, a Brevard County resident. A person fishing in the area found Thompson's body. The second body, a heavily decomposed 65-year-old man, was found Wednesday afternoon shortly after 4 p.m. in shrubbery along the east shoreline near 14510 US Highway 1, just north of Sebastian and across the street from Monday's location.

Sheriff Eric Flowers said Thompson had been staying with his girlfriend at a hotel in Sebastian and was last seen Sunday around 1:30 p.m. walking northbound on U.S. Highway 1. Flowers said Thompson had a history of fentanyl use and mental health issues and had been to mental health facilities in Brevard County many times. The sheriff said Thompson made a purchase of methamphetamine on July 3 and had gone into a manic state. According to Flowers, there was only a minor contusion on Thompson's eyebrow and no violence. The 65-year-old man had a temporary address with his brother in Sebastian and was out of jail on pretrial release after being arrested by Plantation police on an aggravated battery with a deadly weapon charge in Broward County. Flowers said Plantation police was in the process of or had just obtained a warrant for him for absconding on his pretrial release. The man had a serious history of seizures, and his brother took him to a hospital Sunday. Flowers said the man walked away from the hospital against medical advice Sunday morning at 7:30 a.m., still wearing hospital socks and telling his brother he was not going back.

Flowers said autopsies on both bodies revealed no stab wounds or signs of violence. The sheriff said the investigation remains active until toxicology results determine the cause of death. He expressed concern that bad fentanyl or methamphetamine could be on the streets and urged drug users to seek treatment. "Obviously we have nothing that leads us to believe that this is anything but two random incidents that unfortunately happened in the same area," Flowers said. Jim Sullivan, who lives in the area, said the community is usually low crime and docile. He said the two bodies were found about a football field's length apart within a straight line of sight from his bedroom window.

Both cases are still considered suspicious. Flowers said any death that is not a natural death is suspicious and that investigators will continue working to determine what happened. If drug-related issues are involved, the sheriff said his office wants to find out who sold the drugs. Anyone with information is asked to contact the Indian River County Sheriff's Office or Treasure Coast Crime Stoppers.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie ranks 67th most stressed city in U.S., cited for financial stress
cards.teaser: Port St. Lucie ranked as the 67th most stressed city in the United States and is the 42nd most financially stressed city in America, according to a new WalletHub study.
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie ranked as the 67th most stressed city in the United States in a new study released this month by WalletHub. The report cited the city as the 42nd most financially stressed in America. The study compared 182 cities across 39 metrics, which included average weekly work hours, unemployment rate, divorce and suicide rates.

Jacksonville is the most stressed city in Florida, topping out at number 37 in the United States. In South Florida, Miami was on the list at number 50, with affordable housing ranked fourth worst in the United States, and Fort Lauderdale at number 83. WalletHub analyst Chip Lupo said where you live can play a big role in how stressed you are. Cities with high crime rates, weak economies, less effective public health and congested transportation systems naturally lead to elevated stress levels for residents. The report found that money, health and the economy all remain top stressors.

cards.body:
The St. Lucie Mets committed five errors and gave up 17 hits in a 15-3 loss to the Jupiter Hammerheads on Camp Day at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium on Thursday afternoon.

Jupiter scored in each of its final seven innings at the plate, steadily pulling away after the Mets grabbed an early lead.

Antonio Jimenez put St. Lucie ahead 2-1 with a two-run homer in the third inning, his second home run in the last three games and his fifth of the season with the Mets. The lead did not last. Jupiter answered with four runs in the bottom of the third to go up 5-2, keyed by a two-run single from Max Williams and an RBI double from Nixon Chirinos.

Jackson Hauge trimmed the deficit to 5-3 with a two-out RBI single in the fourth, but that was the last Mets hit until Elian Peña singled with one out in the eighth. In between, Jupiter reliever Elier Morillo retired all 10 batters he faced, striking out seven.

The Hammerheads kept adding on, scoring two in the fourth, two in the fifth and four in the sixth, the last punctuated by a three-run homer from Chirinos off Caden Wooster.

All nine Jupiter starters reached base and eight collected hits. Leadoff man Luis Cova went 4 for 5, a triple shy of the cycle, while Williams finished 2 for 5 with a homer, three RBI and three runs. For St. Lucie, Peña, Branny De Oleo and Francisco Toledo each went 2 for 4.

Mets starter Christian Rodriguez took the loss, charged with five runs on eight hits over three innings. He did not walk a batter and struck out five.

The Mets (4-12, 37-45) and Hammerheads (7-11, 44-40) continue their series Friday at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium, with first pitch set for 6:30 p.m.

cards.headline: Florida's updated Live Local Act takes effect, expanding affordable housing opportunities
cards.teaser: An updated version of Florida's Live Local Act took effect today, expanding affordable housing opportunities across the state.
cards.body:
The revised Live Local Act became effective Thursday, introducing changes to Florida's affordable housing framework. The law expands opportunities for affordable housing development statewide.

The implementation has sparked debate at the local level. Communities across Florida are weighing the expanded housing opportunities against local planning concerns as the new provisions take effect.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce art teacher Andre Barnes killed in shooting, family member arrested
cards.teaser: Andre Leonard Barnes, a 66-year-old art teacher, was shot and killed Tuesday afternoon near the 2700 block of Essex Drive in Fort Pierce.
cards.body:
Andre Leonard Barnes, a 66-year-old art teacher, was shot and killed Tuesday afternoon near the 2700 block of Essex Drive in Fort Pierce. The shooting led to the arrest of 41-year-old Dale Mincey, a family member of Barnes. Barnes worked as an art teacher for the St. Lucie County School District since 2017, serving at West Gate K-8 and Samuel S. Gaines Academy. The district confirmed his passing and extended condolences to his loved ones. Barnes leaves behind three adult children.

Barnes' family released a statement asking people to refrain from speculation or public commentary online discussing any other details as the active investigation continues. Former student Caila Coleman, who said Barnes was her 7th-grade teacher in Tallahassee, remembered him as a pillar of the community and father figure to students who didn't grow up with dads. Coleman, now 37 years old, said Barnes made a lifelong impact and that they kept communication well before social media came around, which says a lot about his character. Coleman and others are calling for justice as the homicide investigation remains ongoing.

cards.headline: Park Vista Football Cobras Eye State Playoffs After Strong 2025 Finish
cards.body:
Park Vista Community High School's football team is building on late-season momentum as the Cobras set their sights on the state playoffs in 2026. The team struggled to find its footing early in 2025 but finished strong, winning four of their last five games.

"Felt good throughout the second half of that season," senior Harris Bender said. "We're just working towards being able to carry that through the whole season, like you said, and we have all the pieces in place now, it's just about executing." The ultimate goal is the state playoffs and eventually a state title, something the program has not achieved since 2017.

Park Vista head football coach Donald Hanna emphasized the importance of focusing on each individual contest rather than looking too far ahead. "We got to take it one game at a time," Hanna said. "We can't look past anyone. We got to handle business weekly and if we do that, do our job, that'll get us in the playoffs." The coach's approach reflects a measured strategy as the team works to build on its late-season success from 2025.

Senior players expressed confidence in the team's ability to compete for a championship while acknowledging the work required to achieve their goals. "Coming in, I feel like we got the guys that we need to get it done," senior Erik Lee said. "But also, we got to put the work in to get there as well." Senior Justice Jones showed even greater optimism about the team's prospects. "It's going to feel amazing, because I already know it's gonna happen, definitely," Jones said. Park Vista opens the 2026 season on the road against Atlantic in August. The Cobras are focused on executing their game plan weekly to secure a playoff berth and pursue their first state championship since 2017.

cards.headline: Argentina Rallies Past Egypt 3-2 as Messi Scores in World Cup Round of 16
cards.teaser: Lionel Messi scored his eighth goal of the tournament and led Argentina to an improbable comeback victory despite trailing by two goals with only 11 minutes remaining.
cards.body:
Argentina defeated Egypt 3-2 on Tuesday despite trailing by two goals with only 11 minutes of regulation time to play. Lionel Messi scored his record-extending 21st goal at the World Cup in the 83rd minute to level the score at 2-2. Enzo Fernandez scored the winning goal in stoppage time to complete the comeback. Cristian Romero started the rally in the 79th minute. The goal was Messi's eighth of the tournament. Messi was in tears after the final whistle. Fernandez said this is a phenomenal group that never gives up and that four years have passed since Qatar.

Argentina had trailed 2-0 on goals from Yasser Ibrahim and Mostafa Zico. Ibrahim scored in the 15th minute when he got ahead of Lisandro Martinez to meet Marwan Attia's cross and head the ball into the bottom corner. Zico's goal came in the 67th minute. Messi missed a penalty kick in the first half when his shot was saved by Egypt goalkeeper Mostafa Shobeir after Haissem Hassan tripped Nicolas Tagliafico in the box. Messi has now missed four of eight penalty kicks at World Cups. He later hit the post when the score was 1-0. The defending champions will next face either Switzerland or Colombia in the quarterfinals on Saturday in Kansas City, Missouri. Argentina is bidding to become the first team to win back-to-back titles since Brazil did so in 1958 and 1962.

cards.headline: US-Belgium World Cup Match Draws Biggest Soccer Audience in American History
cards.teaser: Monday's United States-Belgium World Cup match drew more than 30 million viewers on Fox Sports, setting a new record for soccer telecasts in U.S. history.
cards.body:
Monday's United States-Belgium World Cup match was the most-watched soccer telecast in U.S. history, Fox Sports reported. According to Fox, the match drew more than 30 million viewers. Viewership peaked at 36 million early in the second half of Monday's match. The United States lost 4-1 to Belgium. Meanwhile, Telemundo said its Spanish-language broadcast reached 12 million viewers, which NBCUniversal said is a record for a U.S. men's national team broadcast. Interest in Monday's match intensified after FIFA announced that Folarin Balogun would be eligible to play against Belgium despite receiving a red card last week against Bosnia and Herzegovina.

The United States' match against Bosnia and Herzegovina also set records. Fox said about 26.4 million viewers tuned in, setting what was then the record for an English-language soccer broadcast in the United States. Telemundo said it drew 9.8 million viewers, the largest Spanish-language audience for a U.S. men's national team match. Fox said last week's Portugal-Croatia match drew more than 11 million viewers, making it the most-watched World Cup match on Fox that did not involve the United States or a final. Fox also said its Mexico-Ecuador broadcast last week drew more than 10 million viewers. Telemundo said its Mexico-England broadcast delivered 23.1 million viewers.

cards.headline: Women's Professional Baseball League Unveils Team Names and Logos
cards.teaser: The Women's Professional Baseball League unveiled the nicknames and logos of its four teams ahead of its inaugural season, with each team name inspired by pioneering women.
cards.body:
The Women's Professional Baseball League on Wednesday unveiled the nicknames and logos of its four teams ahead of its inaugural season, with each team name inspired by pioneering women. Kelsie Whitmore, the star pitcher who was the first overall pick in the WPBL's inaugural draft, will play for the San Francisco Firebells. Mo'ne Davis, the history-making former Little League sensation, will play center field for the Los Angeles Queens, along with veteran Japanese pitcher Ayami Sato. The other teams are the New York Heights and the Boston Hunters.

The WPBL's debut season begins on Aug. 1 in Springfield, Illinois. Games will be played at Robin Roberts Stadium and will run through the second half of September, including a regular season and playoffs. The New York Heights were inspired by Dorothy Irene Height, a pioneering civil rights and women's rights leader from New York. The San Francisco Firebells were inspired by Lillie Hitchcock Coit, known as Firebelle, who was a champion of San Francisco's volunteer firefighters. The Los Angeles Queens were created after Lizzie Murphy, a baseball pioneer known as the Queen of the Diamond. The Boston Hunters are inspired by Harriot K. Hunt, a pioneering Boston physician and women's rights activist.

cards.headline: Justin Bieber, Madonna to Perform at World Cup Final Halftime Show
cards.teaser: Justin Bieber will join fellow headliners Madonna, Shakira and BTS in a Super Bowl-style halftime show during the World Cup final on July 19.
cards.body:
Justin Bieber will join fellow headliners Madonna, Shakira and BTS in the World Cup's star-studded, Super Bowl-style halftime show, FIFA announced Wednesday. Afrobeats star Burna Boy, Venezuelan conductor Gustavo Dudamel and the PS22 Chorus, a choir of elementary school students based in Staten Island, New York, will also perform, the last joined by Coldplay. The 11-minute halftime performance, curated by Coldplay's Chris Martin, will take place during the final outside New York on July 19. The show will support the FIFA Global Citizen Education Fund, which is raising $100 million to help children access education and soccer.

Burna Boy is one-half of this year's official song for the World Cup, "Dai Dai," led by Shakira. The song is a mesh of Afrobeats and Latin rhythms. In one verse, they name famous soccer players and countries competing: "Brazil, Uruguay, Argentina, Colombia," Shakira cheers. "Mexico, Japan, Korea, Netherlands." This year's World Cup halftime performance will also feature some characters from "Sesame Street," as well as Muppets like Kermit and Miss Piggy. While the Super Bowl is famed for its halftime show, such performances are not commonplace in soccer, with events like the Champions League final featuring a pre-match concert.

cards.headline: Karolina Muchova Defeats Coco Gauff to Reach Wimbledon Final
cards.teaser: Karolina Muchova ended Coco Gauff's run at Wimbledon with a 6-2, 1-6, 7-6 (10) victory Thursday that ended with a drama-filled tiebreaker.
cards.body:
Karolina Muchova ended Coco Gauff's run at Wimbledon with a 6-2, 1-6, 7-6 (10) victory Thursday that ended with a drama-filled tiebreaker, to become the fourth Czech woman in the last six years to reach the final of the grass-court Grand Slam. It will be the ninth-ranked Muchova's second Grand Slam final after losing to Iga Swiatek in the 2023 French Open championship match. Muchova could face another Czech player in Saturday's final, with Linda Noskova to play Marta Kostyuk of Ukraine in the other semifinal next on Centre Court. The other Czech women in the Wimbledon final recently were Karolina Pliskova (runner-up in 2021), Marketa Vondrousova (champion in 2023) and Barbora Krejcikova (champion in 2024).

For Gauff, it was still her most successful Wimbledon. Previously, the seventh-ranked American had gone only as far as the fourth round three times, including during her breakthrough run as a 15-year-old in 2019. The men's semifinals on Friday feature top-ranked and defending champion Jannik Sinner against seven-time Wimbledon winner Novak Djokovic and French Open champion Alexander Zverev against British wild card Arthur Fery.

hero.headline: 18th Annual Treasure Coast Seafood Festival Returns to Vero Beach This November
hero.body:
The 18th Annual Treasure Coast Seafood Festival will return to Vero Beach this November, according to Under The Sun Promotions, Inc.

The festival has become a staple event in Indian River County, drawing seafood lovers from across the Treasure Coast each year. Under The Sun Promotions organizes the annual event.

The festival typically features fresh seafood, live entertainment, and family activities at a Vero Beach waterfront location. Organizers announced the festival's return for November 2026.

Under The Sun Promotions has produced the Treasure Coast Seafood Festival for 18 consecutive years, making it one of the region's longest-running culinary events.

hero.headline: Port St. Lucie ranks 67th most stressed city in nation, study finds
hero.teaser: WalletHub ranked Port St. Lucie as the 67th most stressed city in the United States, citing high financial stress among residents.
hero.body:
WalletHub released a study this month comparing 182 cities across 39 metrics including average weekly work hours, unemployment rate, divorce and suicide rates. Port St. Lucie ranked as the 67th most stressed city in the nation and the 42nd most financially stressed city in America. Compared to other states, Florida performed fairly well overall, with no cities appearing in the top 35 most stressed locations.

Jacksonville topped Florida's list as the most stressed city in the state at number 37 nationally. In South Florida, Miami ranked 50th nationally with the fourth worst affordable housing in the country, and Fort Lauderdale ranked 83rd. Detroit, Baltimore, Cleveland, Memphis and Shreveport, Louisiana topped the list of most stressed cities nationwide.

WalletHub analyst Chip Lupo said cities with high crime rates, weak economies, less effective public health and congested transportation systems naturally lead to elevated stress levels for residents. He noted that while some stress comes from issues with family, friends or employers that are beyond individual control, location plays a significant role in stress levels. Lupo emphasized that when moving, people should consider how a city may impact their mental health, not just their financial opportunities. The report found that money, health and the economy all remain top stressors.

For those seeking less stressful environments, the study identified Fremont, California in the Bay Area as the least stressed city in the nation, despite being a notably affluent area with average home prices of about $1.5 million. South Burlington, Vermont followed in second place, with Bismarck and Fargo, North Dakota rounding out the top locations for low stress levels.
